answer_2.quote: We use the automatic metrics of ROUGE scores . In Table , 4, 5, 6, and 7, we report the unigram overlap (ROUGE-1), bigram overlap (ROUGE-2) to assess informativeness, and longest common subsequence (ROUGE-L) for the fluency of the generated summary.

answer_4.quote: In the first experiment, we presented summaries of PEGASUS , BART , our model, and the gold summary, then asked four professional English speakers to rate the summaries from worst to best in terms of informativeness, faithfulness, topic coherence, and fluency.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators rate each generated summary on multiple criteria (informativeness, faithfulness, topic coherence, fluency) and also participate in a QA style assessment where correctness of answers to questions about the source document is measured.
